leads.summary: The Flatpak sample is staged in a directory that Flatpak does not export to
leads.consequence: A real Flatpak Firefox desktop ID (org.mozilla.firefox.desktop) can be returned by the default-browser lookup, but user exports live under ~/.local/share/flatpak/exports/share/applications and system exports under /var/lib/flatpak/exports/share/applications; neither is searched. The fallback passes org.mozilla.firefox.desktop as a command to uwsm-app, not flatpak run, so this PR's showcased installation still cannot launch from its real export. The synthetic fixture instead places flatpak-firefox.desktop directly under ~/.local/share/applications. This path limitation predates this PR, but defeats its claimed Flatpak support; address the lookup as part of this fix. Current quattro's default-browser helper already searches XDG_DATA_HOME and XDG_DATA_DIRS, exacerbating the lookup/launcher mismatch on rebase.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2 (Flatpak exports not found); published

leads.summary: Substring classifier turns Chromium private launches into normal ones for a browser profile called Firefox
leads.consequence: The regex checks the entire Exec line, including options and user directory names, not just the browser executable. A Chromium desktop entry Exec=chromium --profile-directory=Firefox %U receives --private-window instead of --incognito when called with --private. This is a regression from selecting by browser executable: the requested private window is not requested using Chromium's private flag. The same substring problem applies to 'edge' inside unrelated options. Limit family detection to the executable/app ID, not arbitrary options.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F3 (private flag from whole Exec line); published in More findings

leads.summary: Rebase must preserve default-browser selection and running-browser handoff
leads.consequence: Current quattro uses omarchy-cmd-default-browser, which checks XDG config/data dirs and installed commands, and first attempts omarchy-cmd-browser-handoff for an already-running Chromium before spawning a second process. PR head replaces both helpers with xdg-settings and always spawns, in both launchers. Mechanical git merge-file finds two conflict hunks in the browser launcher and one in the webapp launcher. The PR test on its own head passes without the new helpers, so it cannot protect the handoff after rebase; current quattro's test asserts that a successful handoff produces no systemd-run. Integrate the parsed cmd array with the helpers, retaining the wrapper rejection inside the handoff helper and a full launch fallback.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus rebase section; published in More findings

leads.summary: The new webapp test passes when the webapp fix is entirely removed
leads.consequence: The sole added webapp case writes Exec=chromium ...; touch and checks only that touch was not executed. The pre-PR launcher already reads just the first token 'chromium' and never evaluates the remainder, so it passes this assertion despite still discarding env/flatpak wrappers and every Exec argument. Replace/add a supported Chromium desktop ID (for example brave-browser.desktop) with Exec=/usr/bin/env VAR=1 brave %U, and assert exact argv reaching the setsid/uwsm-app stub including the wrapper, browser and --app. Assert argument boundaries with printf '%s\n' "$@" rather than '$*'.
leads.triage: factual, verified from pr.diff (webapp log never read) and Opus run 10; published as optional test note

leads.summary: #13879 explicitly excludes wrappers that this PR promises to support
leads.consequence: Both branches modify the same webapp launcher and the three-way merged file has two conflict hunks. #13879's browser_command deliberately rejects 'env' at the first Exec token when deciding if a browser is installed (and its test asserts that behavior), while this PR's new parser deliberately supports env-wrapped browser Exec. A resolution preserving #13879's filter would bypass an installed env-wrapped Chrome/Brave and launch a different browser (or report none), rendering this webapp fix ineffective for that example. Its exclusion is an intentional policy in the other PR, so resolve eligibility deliberately rather than treating it as its bug.
leads.triage: factual, verified from related/13879.diff (bare env exclusion); Opus merge-tree confirmed conflict; listed in related-PRs block

leads.summary: Another open Chrome crash fix requires removing the --help probe, which remains here
leads.consequence: For the ordinary Chrome Exec=/usr/bin/google-chrome-stable %U, the fallback branch always calls the browser's --help, even for a non-private URL. Open #12841 removes exactly this probe, reporting that Chrome execs man and crashes when man-db is absent (Omarchy normally installs man-db from install/omarchy-base.packages:78). These diverged PR heads both modify the same condition; their merge-file has one conflict hunk. Without incorporating its no-probe rule, merging this PR would leave that reported failure unfixed. The reported SIGTRAP environment is attributed to #12841, not reproduced here.
leads.triage: factual, verified from related/12841.diff (removes --help probe); Opus merge-tree confirmed conflict; listed in related-PRs block

leads.summary: Overlapping open fixes for both launchers need consolidation
leads.consequence: #12533 implements both wrappers and adds a separate webapp wrapper fixture; #13240 fixes issue #11718 in the browser launcher and #13241 fixes issue #10988 in the webapp launcher. All heads diverge from this PR, and three-way merges conflict in the same launcher functions, not just unrelated lines. Select and reconcile one implementation; merging both without resolving overlapping parser/argument handling gives duplicate or contradictory logic. This is an integration conflict, not a claim that any one PR's design is wrong.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus related-PR section; published in related-PRs block

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The Exec parser splits quoted arguments, and installed Flatpak browsers are still not found.

### Quoted Exec arguments are split

`parse_exec_line` splits at spaces inside quotes, so `"/opt/Example Browser/chromium"` becomes two arguments in both launchers. **Impact:** entries quoting a path or argument with a space launch the wrong command.

**Suggested change:** `elif [[ ($char == ' ' || $char == $'\t') && $in_single -eq 0 && $in_double -eq 0 ]]; then`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at d87d9f8)</summary>

Save as `test/shell.d/launch-browser-quoted-exec-test.sh` and run it with `bash`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT

mock_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
test_home="$test_tmp/home"
mkdir -p "$mock_bin" "$test_home/.local/share/applications"

# Log one argument per line, so argument boundaries are visible.
cat >"$mock_bin/systemd-run" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' "$@" >"$OMARCHY_TEST_LAUNCH"
SH
cp "$mock_bin/systemd-run" "$mock_bin/setsid"
cat >"$mock_bin/xdg-settings" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
echo chromium.desktop
SH
cat >"$mock_bin/omarchy-hyprland-focus-app" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
exit 0
SH
chmod +x "$mock_bin"/*

# Desktop Entry spec, "The Exec key": an argument containing a space is quoted
# in whole and passed to the program as one argument.
cat >"$test_home/.local/share/applications/chromium.desktop" <<'EOF'
[Desktop Entry]
Exec="/opt/Example Browser/chromium" "--user-data-dir=/tmp/Example Profile" %U
EOF

problems=""
for launcher in omarchy-launch-browser omarchy-launch-webapp; do
  log="$test_tmp/$launcher"
  HOME="$test_home" PATH="$mock_bin:$PATH" OMARCHY_TEST_LAUNCH="$log" \
    bash "$ROOT/bin/$launcher" "https://example.test/quoted"
  if ! grep -Fxq -- '/opt/Example Browser/chromium' "$log" ||
    ! grep -Fxq -- '--user-data-dir=/tmp/Example Profile' "$log"; then
    problems+="$launcher ran:"$'\n'"$(sed -n '/^--$/,$p' "$log" | tail -n +2)"$'\n'
  fi
done

[[ -z $problems ]] || fail "launchers keep quoted Exec arguments whole" "$problems"
pass "launchers keep quoted Exec arguments whole"
```

Output at `d87d9f8` (exit status 1):

```
omarchy-launch-browser ran:
/opt/Example
Browser/chromium
--user-data-dir=/tmp/Example
Profile
https://example.test/quoted
omarchy-launch-webapp ran:
/opt/Example
Browser/chromium
--user-data-dir=/tmp/Example
Profile
--app=https://example.test/quoted

not ok - launchers keep quoted Exec arguments whole
```

With the suggested change it prints `ok - launchers keep quoted Exec arguments whole`, and the PR's own test still passes.
</details>

### Installed Flatpak browsers are not found

Flatpak exports entries to `XDG_DATA_DIRS` paths the lookup never searches, so the fallback runs `uwsm-app -- org.mozilla.firefox.desktop --private-window URL`. **Impact:** uwsm makes the flag a `file://` URL, so `--private URL` opens the URL in a normal window.

**Suggested change:** also search `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `XDG_DATA_DIRS`, and refuse private launches when only the desktop ID is known.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at d87d9f8)</summary>

Save as `test/shell.d/launch-browser-flatpak-export-test.sh` and run it with `bash`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT

mock_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
test_home="$test_tmp/home"
# Flatpak exports desktop files here (added to XDG_DATA_DIRS), not to
# ~/.local/share/applications.
exports="$test_home/.local/share/flatpak/exports/share/applications"
mkdir -p "$mock_bin" "$exports"

cat >"$mock_bin/systemd-run" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' "$@" >"$OMARCHY_TEST_LAUNCH"
SH
cat >"$mock_bin/xdg-settings" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
echo org.mozilla.firefox.desktop
SH
cat >"$mock_bin/omarchy-hyprland-focus-app" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
exit 0
SH
chmod +x "$mock_bin"/*

# The Exec line Flatpak writes for an exported Firefox.
cat >"$exports/org.mozilla.firefox.desktop" <<'EOF2'
[Desktop Entry]
Exec=/usr/bin/flatpak run --branch=stable --arch=x86_64 --command=firefox --file-forwarding org.mozilla.firefox @@u %u @@
EOF2

launch_log="$test_tmp/launch"
# Flatpak's env.d adds its export dirs to XDG_DATA_DIRS the same way.
HOME="$test_home" PATH="$mock_bin:$PATH" OMARCHY_TEST_LAUNCH="$launch_log" \
  XDG_DATA_DIRS="$test_home/.local/share/flatpak/exports/share:/usr/local/share:/usr/share" \
  bash "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-launch-browser" --private "https://example.test/private"

command=$(sed -n '/^--$/{n;p;q}' "$launch_log")
[[ $command == /usr/bin/flatpak ]] ||
  fail "browser launcher runs the Exec of an exported Flatpak browser" "$(sed -n '/^--$/,$p' "$launch_log")"
pass "browser launcher runs the Exec of an exported Flatpak browser"
```

Output at `d87d9f8` (exit status 1):

```
--
org.mozilla.firefox.desktop
--private-window
https://example.test/private
not ok - browser launcher runs the Exec of an exported Flatpak browser
```

What `uwsm-app` expands that fallback to, run with `python3` on an Omarchy install (uwsm and python-pyxdg installed):

```python
import sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(1, "/usr/share/uwsm/modules")  # where the uwsm package installs its modules
from xdg.DesktopEntry import DesktopEntry
from uwsm.main import gen_entry_args

# What `uwsm-app -- org.mozilla.firefox.desktop --private-window <url>` expands to.
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".desktop") as entry:
    entry.write("[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nName=Firefox\n"
                "Exec=/usr/bin/flatpak run --branch=stable --arch=x86_64 --command=firefox "
                "--file-forwarding org.mozilla.firefox @@u %u @@\n")
    entry.flush()
    command, instances = gen_entry_args(DesktopEntry(entry.name), ["--private-window", "https://example.test/private"])
    for args in instances:
        print(command, *args)
```

Output (uwsm 0.26.7-1, python-pyxdg 0.28-7):

```
/usr/bin/flatpak run --branch=stable --arch=x86_64 --command=firefox --file-forwarding org.mozilla.firefox @@u file://--private-window @@
/usr/bin/flatpak run --branch=stable --arch=x86_64 --command=firefox --file-forwarding org.mozilla.firefox @@u https://example.test/private @@
```

Looking the entry up through `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `~/.nix-profile/share` and `XDG_DATA_DIRS` makes this test pass; when `XDG_DATA_HOME` is set in the environment, the PR's test then also needs `export XDG_DATA_HOME="$test_home/.local/share"`, as `quattro`'s version has.
</details>

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

**Conflicts with `quattro`.** #13520 and #13530 changed both launchers, and #13530 the test, adding `omarchy-cmd-default-browser` and `omarchy-cmd-browser-handoff`. **Impact:** the branch does not apply to current `quattro`, and a resolution that keeps the PR's lookup block would undo #13520. **Suggested change:** rebase, keeping `omarchy-cmd-default-browser` and passing the parsed `"${cmd[@]}"` to `omarchy-cmd-browser-handoff` before the existing launch fallback.

Checked resolution: `if ! omarchy-cmd-browser-handoff "${cmd[@]}"; then systemd-run ... uwsm-app -- "${cmd[@]}"; fi` (webapp: same with `--app="$1" "${@:2}"` and `exec setsid`). A hand rebase done this way passes the merged test (with the checkout's `bin` on `PATH`).

**Private flag is picked from the whole Exec line.** The Mozilla/`edge` regexes scan every argument and the `--help` probe runs the wrapper, so `env MOZ_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1 zen %u` gets `--incognito` (wrapped entries failed completely before) and `brave --profile-directory=Ledger` gets `--inprivate` (the base sent `--incognito`). **Impact:** the browser gets another browser's private flag, so the private request is lost. **Suggested change:** detect from the resolved browser token (skip `env` and `VAR=val`, use the Flatpak app ID).
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- `env VAR=val brave %U` and Flatpak-style Exec lines in `~/.local/share/applications` now launch the full command in both launchers.
- Native Chromium, Chrome, Brave, Edge, Firefox and Zen entries get the same argv and focus regex as before, except `URL --private` is reordered to `--private-flag URL` and extra URLs are dropped.
- No `eval`; the metacharacter Exec stays literal.
- The PR test passes at the head and fails on the base scripts at the Flatpak assertion.

**Optional notes:**
- The webapp case only checks that no file was created and never reads `OMARCHY_TEST_WEBAPP_LAUNCH`, so the test also passes with the original webapp launcher restored. Asserting the argv of an `env ... brave %U` entry would cover #10988.
- The mocks log `"$*"`, which hides argument boundaries (the first finding); logging `"$@"` one per line would expose them.
</details>

<details><summary>Other open PRs for this issue</summary>

- #13240: browser launcher only; double-quote-aware tokenizer that keeps quoted spaces, `%f`/`%F` also take the URL, extra arguments kept.
- #12533: both launchers (fixes #10988); splits with `read -r -a`, no quote handling.
- #13241: webapp counterpart of #13240 (fixes #10988).
- #13879 skips webapp entries whose command is a bare `env`, and #12841 removes the `--help` probe; both conflict with this PR's changes to the same lines.
</details>
